clue.text: Withstand appalling dangers where there's tumult

parts.note: to bear something is to withstand or endure it

indicators.note: appalling suggests the word dangers is in a dreadful mess, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to stand firm against terrible perils in a riotous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appalling' rearranges DANGERS into GARDENS, which follows BEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bear garden was a place for baiting bears, and the phrase now names any scene of noisy disorder.

clue.text: Hounds the sportsmen holding a letter up

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other within it

parts.note: bats are batsmen, players in cricket

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ess is the spelt-out name of the letter S

explanation.surface: Some sportsmen carry a letter while chasing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ESS into SSE, and 'holding' puts that inside BATS. 'Hounds' looks like a verb but is the plural noun for the dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bassets are a breed of short-legged dog used for hunting by scent.

clue.text: A US lawyer writing as a former president

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American public prosecutor
MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An American attorney writes in the guise of an ex-president.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were both early presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Not the Emerald Isle!

parts.note: Ireland is called the Emerald Isle, a green country; the clue points to a different island whose name also suggests green territory but is mostly ice

explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the island's name describes Ireland better than itself, being largely covered in ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The world's largest island, in the Arctic, is named for verdant country it hardly resembles, unlike Ireland.

clue.text: Back the right hearing device

parts.note: the ear is the organ we hear with

explanation.surface: Someone supports the correct hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of something is its hind part or tail end.

clue.text: People rowing about acquiescence can make sense

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
saying yes shows acquiescence or agreement

explanation.surface: Rowers agreeing to something shows good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts EIGHT around YES. 'rowing' suggests arguing, but it means people in boats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Good quality stuff- Russian

definitions.meaning: stuff is old word for cloth, and this is a hard-wearing twilled woollen fabric
the French form of the Russian name Sergei, borne by men such as the ballet impresario Diaghilev

explanation.definitionFit: Serge is a durable twilled cloth, and it is also a Russian man's given name in its French form.

clue.text: Many taking less fat will appear more presentable

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so it stands for many
leaner means having less fat

explanation.surface: Lots of people who go on diets will look smarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cleaner, with less dirt, makes someone neater and more fit to be seen.

clue.text: A period of perpetual spring?

parts.note: spring is read as jumping rather than the season, a whole year spent bounding about

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an endless season of blossom; the clue really means a year of leaping.
explanation.definitionFit: A year of 366 days, with an extra day in February, is named for jumping.

clue.text: Jaded fellow seeing no advantage either way

parts.note: stale means jaded, tired from overuse
a mate is a fellow or companion

explanation.surface: A weary companion finds that neither side is gaining ground.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is a drawn position where neither player can win, hence a deadlock.

clue.text: Set about the first woman magistrate!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
in the Bible, Eve is the first woman

explanation.surface: Someone sets about appointing the first female magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' just asks you to place RE before EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with powers like a magistrate's or bailiff's.

clue.text: In age maybe find some vice comforting

indicators.note: In means one piece is placed inside the other
maybe says the word age is only one possible order of its letters

parts.note: the word age taken as letters to rearrange
a sin is a vice or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Someone in old age finds comfort in a few bad habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AGE into EAG, and 'In' puts SIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Easing pain or worry soothes, which is what comforting does.

clue.text: Over-subtle play upon words after penalties

indicators.note: after means the second piece follows the first in the answer

parts.note: fines are monetary penalties
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Someone makes a pun following the punishments handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finespun is spun very thin, so figuratively too delicate or refined in argument.

clue.text: Drapes material for display

indicators.note: material suggests the word Drapes is the raw stuff, its letters to be made up into something new

explanation.surface: Curtain fabric is laid out for show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' tells you to rearrange the letters of DRAPES.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish array, such as a feast laid out or a full-page show in a magazine.

clue.text: Dwelling to be rented is renovated

indicators.note: renovated means done up afresh, so the letters of rented is are remade

explanation.surface: A home available to let has been refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resident in a place is living there, so dwelling is an adjective sense.

clue.text: A flier requires warmth in clothing

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: wear is clothing, as in menswear
heat means warmth

explanation.surface: An airman needs heat inside his garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts HEAT inside WEAR. 'A flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small songbird, a thrush-like chat with a white rump.

clue.text: Expect to pick up

definitions.meaning: an older sense means to anticipate, often with dread
the police pick up a suspect when they arrest them

explanation.definitionFit: Apprehend means to arrest a suspect, and in an older sense to anticipate something with fear.

clue.text: Changed course, 80 could well be beaten

definitions.meaning: to have ... is to have changed direction
a switch is a thin cane, so being ... means being whipped with one

explanation.walkthrough: The '80' in the clue as held is probably 'so' misread from the printed page; it does nothing in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To be switched is to have changed course, or to have been thrashed with a supple cane.

clue.text: Found one area of Ireland depressed

parts.note: to found metal is to cast it in a mould
Down is a county in Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a part of Ireland that is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning to cast metal. DOWN is a county of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cast down is to be dejected or low in spirits.

clue.text: Person cutting short becoming a failure

definitions.meaning: someone who crops hair or plants, trimming them short

explanation.definitionFit: One who crops things is a trimmer, and to come a cropper means to fall heavily or fail.

clue.text: The city's left going in circles

indicators.note: going in means one piece enters the other

parts.note: two circles look like two letter O shapes
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A city where everyone travelling seems to move round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going in' puts PORT between the two Os. The 's of 'city's' is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is the old English name for Porto, Portugal's second-largest city.

clue.text: Noisily exercises in a wood when not busy

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the other

parts.note: oak is a type of wood
ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction to play very loudly
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone works out loudly in a forest when nobody else is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts FF and PE inside OAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-peak times are those outside the rush, with less demand.

clue.text: A doubter can be quite difficult to influence

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters of A doubter may be turned into another word

explanation.surface: A sceptic can be very hard to persuade.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly unyielding, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Name harp-maker to receive the sovereign

indicators.note: to receive means one piece takes the other inside it
maker suggests the word harp is made into something new from its letters

parts.note: the word harp taken as letters to rearrange
a sovereign is a gold coin worth a pound, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A harp builder is paid in gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maker' rearranges HARP into RAPH, and 'to receive' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's first name.

clue.text: Discharged to show clemency

definitions.meaning: a gun or firework that is fired has gone off

explanation.definitionFit: A firework let off is discharged, and to let someone off is to spare them punishment.

clue.text: Decoration in stone of a golden colour

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed within the second

parts.note: ore is mineral-bearing rock
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order awarded as a decoration

explanation.surface: A medal set in a golden-coloured gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CH inside ORE. CH, Companion of Honour, is a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy pigment, a yellowish-brown or golden shade.

clue.text: Some disciplinarians like such a song

indicators.note: Some means only a part of the word disciplinarians is taken

explanation.surface: A few strict teachers enjoy that kind of song.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: Having to write a number is really punishing

parts.note: to pen is to write
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Having to write a figure is a real torment.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal means relating to punishment, as in penal servitude.

clue.text: Mounts weed as 8 good-luck token

parts.note: horses are mounts for riding
to hoe is to weed the ground

explanation.surface: Riders tend their gardens to bring fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The '8' in the clue as held is the word 'a' misread from the printed page, a link with 'as'.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe hung over a door is a traditional charm for luck.

clue.text: Youngsters may be found playing the game

definitions.text: Youngsters may be found playing the game

parts.words: Youngsters may be found playing the game
parts.note: in this children's game some players conceal themselves and are found by the seeker

explanation.walkthrough: 'found' does double duty: children are discovered while playing this game.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's game where one player looks for the others who have concealed themselves.
